newsitem.title: USA: Union Texas raising 1997 capital spending.
newsitem.headline: Union Texas raising 1997 capital spending.

text.p: Union Texas Petroleum Holdings Inc said Monday its 1997 capital spending budget will rise to $269 million from its original 1997 capital budget of $229 million.
Union Texas said the 17 percent increase is for several new exploration ventures that it has recently joined.
It said with the increase, its revised 1997 capital budget represents a 45 percent boost over $186 million spent in 1996.
The company said the majority of the increased capital budget for 1997 is earmarked for three new exploration ventures in Kazakstan, Algeria and China.

The company recently announced it has formed a joint venture with Oman Oil Co Ltd to explore for, develop and produce oil and natural gas onshore Kazakstan and offshore in the Kazakstan sector of the Caspian Sea.

Union Texas said it has also recently joined subsidiaries of Phillips Petroleum Co in exploration ventures in the Ghadames Basin in southeastern Algeria and Bohai Bay offshore northern China. Union Texas has a 75 percent working interest in the Kazakstan/Caspian Sea venture, a 30 percent working interest in the Algerian venture, and a four percent working interest in the China venture.

Union Texas said that overall, it is increasing its 1997 capital spending plans for its worldwide exploration ventures from about $68 million to about $95 million, about 35 percent of the revised 1997 capital budget.
In addition to the ventures in Kazakstan, Algeria and China, the increased exploration budget includes monies for new programs in Yemen and Latin America.
